nodes.name: Retrieval Validation & Metadata Filtering
nodes.notes: Retrieval Validation & Metadata Filtering: This node's responsibility is to act as a gate between Workflow 3's output and the ranking logic — it checks that the upstream retrieval actually succeeded (search_status === 'ok', retrieval_status.status === 'SUCCESS'), re-verifies that every chunk's similarity score still clears the threshold (defense in depth, since we can't blindly trust an upstream flag after having just found a real bug in that upstream step), and applies any caller-supplied metadata filters (department, category, document, etc.) if present. We used a separate node for this rather than folding it into ranking because validation and filtering are a different concern from scoring — one decides what evidence is even eligible to be considered, the other decides how eligible evidence is ordered. Keeping them separate also means Workflow 8's logging can capture validation failures (bad threshold, upstream error, empty result set) independently of ranking failures, which matters for debugging exactly the kind of pipeline bug we just found.

nodes.name: Composite Ranking & Diversity Engine
nodes.notes: Composite Ranking & Diversity Engine: This node's responsibility is to take the validated chunk set and produce an ordered, diversity-enforced evidence list — computing a weighted composite score per chunk (similarity plus structural and recency proxies) and then applying a per-document cap so a single source document can't dominate the top results. We used a separate node here because ranking and diversity are themselves two distinct operations bundled for practical reasons: ranking decides how good each chunk is, diversity decides how the good chunks get distributed across documents, and both need to happen after validation has already guaranteed the input is trustworthy. Splitting this from Node 1 also means the ranking weights and diversity caps can be tuned or A/B tested without touching the validation/filtering logic at all — a change to RANKING_WEIGHTS doesn't risk breaking threshold checks, and vice versa. This node is explicitly barred from prompt building or LLM calls, per the architecture's separation of concerns — its only output is ranked_evidence and analytics for Workflow 5 to consume.
